SIKA® BLOCK: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® Block, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/g/sika_block.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® Block where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. Sika® Block is a biodegradable synthetic based admixture for masonry block manufacture. Sika® Block is designed for use with zero or low slump concrete commonly used in the manufacture of masonry blocks.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Sika® Block is utilised where an improvement in appearance of the masonry unit is required. This is achieved by creating better slick, improving moldability, enhancing cohesion and increasing early age strength.
    - Sika® Block performs best when added to low slump masonry block mixes. It provides a more efficient utilisation of mixing water by aiding the dispersion of cement particles. Sika® Block will also improve the appearance and density of masonry units.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.3.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® Block
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Masonry Block and Paver Admixture
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.02) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Improved Workability and Finishing as well as Appearance
    - Plasticises for a better slick
    - Reduces Tear and Wear on Machinery
    - Reduced shrinkage
    - Higher production rates
    - By increasing the production rates, cost reduction will be achieved
    - Maintaining the long term appearance as well as strength
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Appearance and colour: Blue liquid
    - Specific gravity: 1.01 g/cm ³
2.5 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: Bulk deliveries; 1000 litre IBC; 205 litre drum; 10 litre container
    - Shelf life: Stored at temperatures between 5°C and 35°C in unopened original containers protected from direct sunlight and frost, shelf life is one (1) year.
    - Storage conditions: Store at temperature between 5° and 35°, protected from direct sunlight.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.02) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Recommended dosage: Sika® Block can be used at rates of 150-500mls per 100kg of total cementitious material. Optimum dosage should be determined by site trials.
    - Dispensing: Sika® Block should be added with mixing water to ensure correct dispersion and maximum performance.
4.3 Limitations and important considerations.
    - When using Sika® Block for air-dried masonry products, curing should be completed before exposure to water or rain.
    - Streaking and discolouring may occur where water has come into contact with masonry products which are not fully cured.
    - For additional information, please contact your local Sika Representative.
4.4 Further information. May slightly increase air content

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.3):
    - When using Sika® Block for air-dried masonry products, curing should be completed before exposure to water or rain.
5.3 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® Block, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/g/sika_block.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sika Block, version 08/11/2022, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/i/Sika%20Block.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
